title: Contract on FFI Functions
concept: Contracts on FFI functions act as safety guards between XIOM's safe world and the unsafe world of C/native code.
why: FFI is the most dangerous part of any systems language. Contracts on FFI boundaries catch invalid data BEFORE it reaches native code.
tips: Every FFI function should have contracts — even if just requires: ptr != null
The contract acts as documentation for what the C function expects
FFI contract violations trap BEFORE entering native code — saving you from segfaults
Use @pre in FFI ensures to verify the C function didn't corrupt your data
common_mistakes: Assuming the C function validates its own inputs — most C functions do NOT
Forgetting that C pointers can be null — always require non-null before passing to C
Writing contracts that can't actually be verified at the boundary
